newsitem.title: USA: Future AT&T CEO makes first management reshuffle.
newsitem.headline: Future AT&T CEO makes first management reshuffle.

text.p: John Walter, the future leader of AT&T Corp., made his first mark on the largest U.S. telecommunications company with a management shuffle Sunday.

Walter, who is to become chief executive officer of AT&T on Jan. 1, 1998, replaced Joseph Nacchio, a 26-year veteran of the company and an architect of AT&T's failed attempt to recover its share of the consumer long-distance market.
He named Gail McGovern in Nacchio's place as executive vice president of the consumer and small business division.
"We need to make a lot of decisions on many fronts and this is one of them," he said in a telephone interview.
McGovern, who served as executive vice president of the business markets division, said in an earlier interview that she would focus on "top-line revenue growth" on assuming her new post.

Walter, whose appointment last October was not well received on Wall Street due to his inexperience in the telecommunications industry, declined to say if he planned to make more changes at the senior executive level.
"I'm comfortable with the level of management that we have now," said Walter, who had worked as chief executive of the commercial printer R.R. Donnelley & Sons Co.
Walter has been working alongside Robert Allen, AT&T's outgoing chief executive officer, to get acquainted with the company since his appointment in October.

Nacchio later said in an interview that he had decided to leave AT&T over the weekend after getting an "offer I couldn't refuse" from Qwest Communications Corp., a small telecommunications firm in Denver.

Nacchio, a company veteran who had worked for AT&T since March 1970, will become president and chief executive officer of Qwest, which designs and builds fiber optic networks as well as manages a national long-distance network.
